title: DuraTail: Detection and Precision Analysis of Tumor Infiltration in the Peripheral Regions of Meningiomas Using AI-Assisted Stimulated Raman Histology (DuraTail_24)
summary: Meningiomas are the most common benign brain tumors. The goal of surgery is complete removal of the tumor including the affected meninges to prevent recurrence. During surgery, however, it is difficult with conventional methods to determine whether the meninges at the tumor margin are still infiltrated by tumor cells or merely appear thickened due to inflammation. In this study, a novel laser technology (stimulated Raman histology) is used that allows small tissue samples to be visualized microscopically within minutes without extensive tissue processing. Based on the images obtained, a computer-based program will be developed that can automatically distinguish between healthy meninges, tumor-infiltrated meninges, and reactively altered meninges. The accuracy of this program will be compared to conventional tissue examination by a pathologist. The surgical procedure itself is not influenced by the study; only a small portion of tissue already removed during surgery is additionally examined using the new method.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Imaging suspicion of primary convexity meningioma and/or recurrent convexity meningioma
Interdisciplinary neuro-oncological tumor board recommendation for resection with Simpson grade I intention (complete removal including dural attachment and involved bone)
Patient has capacity to consent
Patient is undergoing tumor surgery at the neuro-oncological center of the University Hospital of Cologne independent of the study
Written informed consent for study participation
Exclusion criteria:
Absence of consent for study participation
Patient lacks capacity to consent
